title: Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring assortativity coefficients and estimating marginal effects in discrete choice models to determine if LLM agents preferentially connect with nodes that share similar attributes (e.g., hobbies, favorite colors, geographical locations).
Calculating the probability of agents forming links with already high-degree nodes compared to a random baseline, and analyzing the resulting scale-free network degree distributions.
Measuring marginal transitivity and the likelihood of agents connecting to nodes with which they share common neighbors across synthetic environments and real-world network datasets.
Observing heterophilous choices in simulated corporate employment networks by analyzing whether LLM agents acting as subordinates preferentially form links with managers.
